_description: Describes the MeitY chatbot's chat/stream API contract, consumed by capture_new_chatbot.py. The base URL, API key and any extra headers are deliberately NOT hardcoded here - they come from environment variables at runtime (see .env.example).
_confirmed: Confirmed 2026-11-20 via Playwright network capture of a genuine browser session asking a real golden-dataset question (GD-MTY-LS17-2-U2536-V) through the MeitY portal's standalone 'AI Assistant' chat at https://pqa.myscheme.in/meityy/ai-assistant, including a live two-turn follow-up test confirming conversation continuity.
base_url_note: Set to https://pqa.myscheme.in/meityy/api/assistant (confirmed). capture_new_chatbot.py exits with a setup message if PQA_CHATBOT_BASE_URL is unset rather than falling back to any default.

body_template.query: <row's user_input, verbatim - no wrapper prompt for this project, see capture/prompt.py's docstring>
body_template.messages: <[...history turns, {role: user, content: query}] - see capture/client.py's history param>

request.note: Confirmed live: no draft_context/sub_question/part_label here - that was the previous project's different, per-sub-question 'Draft with AI' contract. This is MeitY's general-purpose chat contract. `type` is always the literal string "generate" (confirmed from a real request, not a guess).

auth.status: CONFIRMED as session-cookie based, same mechanism and same email-OTP login flow as the previous project's portal (same myscheme.in platform family, different ministry slug: /meityy vs /comind).
auth.session_file_usage: Path to a Playwright storageState JSON. capture/session.py extracts every cookie whose domain matches PQA_CHATBOT_BASE_URL's host and sends them as a single 'Cookie:' header. No cookie value is ever logged, printed, or written anywhere by this script.
auth.cookie_header_usage: A raw 'Cookie:' header value, for supplying a session directly without a storageState file. Takes precedence over PQA_CHATBOT_SESSION_FILE if both are set.
auth.api_key_usage: Not used for this endpoint - kept as a generic fallback only.
auth.extra_headers_usage: Optional JSON object of additional request headers, merged in as-is.
auth.on_401_403: capture_new_chatbot.py raises CaptureAuthError (not a generic error) and ABORTS THE WHOLE RUN rather than retrying or continuing to the next row - a rejected session will reject every remaining row identically. See README.md 'Supplying a session cookie'.

other_observed_events.status: progress messages, e.g. {"message": "Retrieving sources..."} - ignored by capture
other_observed_events.token: streamed partial answer tokens, e.g. {"token": "..."} - ignored by capture; only the terminal 'complete' event's full answer is captured

source_object_fields.note: CONFIRMED LIVE 2026-11-20: unlike the previous project's endpoint, this one's 'sources' entries carry a genuine `full_text` field (observed 2,000-3,000+ chars) distinct from and much longer than the ~500-char `text_preview` - verified by direct length/content comparison on real captured sources, not assumed. This means retrieved_contexts WILL populate for this project, and Faithfulness/Context Precision/Context Recall will NOT be NA by default the way they were for the previous project - a real, meaningful capability difference. Each source also carries: topic, filename, source_url, s3_url, score, assembly, session_date, question_number, question_type, section_type, answer_reference, contains_table, annexure_id, annexure_page, result_type, pages, chunk_count, document_fingerprint, ministry, answering_minister.

known_from_live_probe.verified_auth: browser session cookie from an email-OTP login; no Authorization header was sent and the call succeeded
known_from_live_probe.verified_response_shape: event: status (x3) -> event: token (many, streamed word-by-word) -> event: complete {"answer": "...", "sources": [{...}], "query": "...", "total_results": N, "query_type": "parliamentary", "llmModel": "in.anthropic.claude-sonnet-5", "embeddingModel": null, "inputs_used": []}
known_from_live_probe.verified_continuity: a second call reusing the same session_id/user_id but WITHOUT replaying history in messages did NOT carry context by itself in testing implication - the real frontend always replays full prior-turn history into messages regardless of session_id, and that replay is what the backend actually used (confirmed: a follow-up correctly resolved 'that Act you mentioned' to the specific Act discussed in the prior turn, citing the correct distinct source document).
known_from_live_probe.note: This block records what was actually observed during manual testing, for traceability. It is informational only - it is never read by capture_new_chatbot.py and must not be treated as a substitute for setting PQA_CHATBOT_BASE_URL / auth configuration explicitly.
